objective: Enforce abuse controls on the public adviser endpoints without ever hard-failing a legitimate task. Per-IP rate limiting stores ONLY an HMAC-hashed IP plus counters in PostgreSQL (never a raw IP). The deterministic endpoints (/adviser/recommend, /adviser/export) return HTTP 429 + Retry-After on per-IP overage. The assisted endpoint (/adviser/recommend/assisted) gracefully DEGRADES to the deterministic fallback (HTTP 200, llm_used=false, clear fallback_reason) whenever the AI path is gated - by the global kill switch, by AI-quota exhaustion, by an open per-provider circuit breaker, or by a missing/failed proof-of-work - and only hard-fails with 429 on an absolute request ceiling. Request dedupe collapses identical concurrent/repeated submissions within a short window so a burst does not multiply LLM calls or burn the rate budget. A self-hosted, server-signed proof-of-work challenge (POST /adviser/challenge) gates expensive assisted requests beyond the free AI threshold. All state (rate buckets, kill switch, breaker, dedupe, PoW issuance) is persisted in PostgreSQL via migration 0008 (down_revision 0007_source_slug), which round-trips cleanly.

acceptance_criteria: 1. Per-IP rate limiting persists ONLY an HMAC-hashed IP (HMAC-SHA256 with a server secret) plus counters/timestamps in PostgreSQL - never a raw client IP. Deterministic (X-Forwarded-For honoured, leftmost).

2. Deterministic endpoints (/adviser/recommend, /adviser/export) return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when a per-IP overage exceeds deterministic_requests_per_ip_per_day; requests within budget return 200.

3. The AI kill switch is persisted in PostgreSQL (abuse_flag) and togglable via the internal CLI; when ON, the assisted path is forced to the deterministic fallback (llm_used=false, fallback_reason=ai_kill_switch) WITHOUT hard-failing, and /adviser/recommend stays fully available.

4. A per-provider circuit breaker opens after N consecutive provider failures/timeouts (cooldown), short-circuits that provider (routing falls through to deterministic fallback), and allows a single half-open probe after cooldown that closes on success or reopens on failure. State persists in PostgreSQL (survives restart; no Redis).

5. Request dedupe collapses identical concurrent/repeated requests within a short window (idempotency by hashing the normalized request body) so a burst of identical submissions does not multiply LLM calls or rate-limit burn; deterministic and testable.

6. A self-hosted proof-of-work challenge (POST /adviser/challenge; server-signed with stdlib HMAC, single-use, expiring) gates expensive/assisted requests beyond the free threshold; the server verifies signature (constant-time), expiry, and work before admitting the request; NO external CAPTCHA. Difficulty is configurable and low for tests.

7. Quota-exhaustion semantics: when the AI/assisted quota is exhausted (rate/kill switch/breaker/missing-PoW) the assisted endpoint DEGRADES to the deterministic fallback (HTTP 200, llm_used=false, clear fallback_reason) rather than erroring; a deterministic overage beyond the per-IP limit returns HTTP 429 + Retry-After. The distinction is explicit and tested. The assisted endpoint only hard-fails (429) on an absolute request ceiling.

8. Migration 0008 (down_revision 0007_source_slug) creates exactly the 5 abuse tables, provides upgrade() and downgrade(), and round-trips clean (up -> down -> up, no drift). Revisions stay linear (0007 -> 0008).

9. No new runtime dependency and no Redis (FastAPI + Python stdlib only); no external network on the LLM path; existing SSRF/reject_urls guards intact; no LLM-to-publication path; no secrets in source/logs/tests/examples; containers keep health checks; amd64/arm64 preserved.
10. Offline gates green: scripts/test.ps1 exit 0 (pytest incl. all new abuse tests + web vitest + vite build) and scripts/check.ps1 -NodeAudit exit 0 (all 8 gates).

risks.data_migration: Migration 0008 (down_revision 0007_source_slug) adds 5 abuse tables and round-trips clean (up -> down -> up, no drift; proven live). Revisions stay linear. No backfill, no destructive change to existing tables.
risks.security_privacy: Only an HMAC-SHA256 hash of the client IP is persisted (raw IP used transiently to compute the hash, never stored or logged). Prompts/descriptions are never logged and consent stays ephemeral (Q2). The proof-of-work challenge is self-hosted and server-signed with stdlib HMAC (Q3/Q6) - no external CAPTCHA, no JWT lib; tokens carry no secret beyond the HMAC signature and are single-use + expiring, verified constant-time. The public endpoints still reject user-controlled URLs (reject_urls) and preserve the SSRF scheme guard. No secrets in source/logs/tests/examples (detect-secrets green; ABUSE_SECRET is a non-secret dev default, pragma-allowlisted).
risks.portability: No new runtime dependency and no Redis (Q9): FastAPI + Python stdlib (hmac, hashlib, secrets, time) + the already-present SQLAlchemy/Alembic only. amd64/arm64 unaffected; containers keep health checks. Circuit-breaker/rate/dedupe/PoW state lives in PostgreSQL so it survives restarts without an extra service.
risks.zero_cost_safety: Abuse controls never re-derive Z0/quota/classification and never hard-fail a legitimate task: the deterministic /adviser/recommend path stays fully available, and the assisted path degrades to the deterministic fallback (200, llm_used=false, clear reason) under kill switch / quota / breaker / missing-PoW. No LLM-to-publication path.
risks.immutability: The 5 abuse tables are additive and orthogonal to the domain catalogue; existing immutability/separation triggers are untouched. Store writes use their own engine.begin() transactions independent of the read-only request session.
risks.regression: Additive: a new abuse/ package + 5 ORM models + migration 0008 + settings knobs + router enforcement + one new /challenge endpoint + additive compose/env/docs + additive tests (existing adviser tests adjusted only to inject an InMemory store). The deterministic adviser core and S1/S3 behaviour are unchanged.
